business_problem: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport needed to absorb a historic expansion and rising passenger volumes while delivering over 20% efficiency in operations and maintenance, improving customer experience, and shifting airport management from reactive response to proactive control.
solution_summary: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport worked with BCG to embed AI directly into frontline operations as it expanded the airport by about 20% and prepared for more than 100 million passengers a year. After a workshop with operations, public safety, maintenance, engineering, and technology teams, the program focused on two production platforms. AWARE (Advanced Warning and Response Exchange) fuses more than 10 real-time data streams and generates over 120,000 predictions a day across 26 key roadways so operations, police, and ground transport can act on congestion before it escalates. In parallel, the Resource Scheduling Optimizer combines workforce availability, maintenance demand, work-order history, sensor data, and condition data on an asset-health foundation, then serves technicians a digital work application, optimized schedules, and an asset-manager cockpit. BCG initially led delivery and then transferred ownership so DFW could operate and extend the platforms itself.

solution_components.name: AWARE (Advanced Warning and Response Exchange)
solution_components.role: Fuses real-time roadway and airport-flow data to generate predictive alerts for congestion and disruption management.

solution_components.name: Resource Scheduling Optimizer
solution_components.role: Plans and dispatches maintenance work by matching workforce availability with maintenance needs.

solution_components.name: asset-health foundation
solution_components.role: Brings together work-order history, sensor data, and asset condition into a single operational data layer.

solution_components.name: asset-manager cockpit
solution_components.role: Gives asset managers a consolidated view for maintenance planning and repair-or-replace decisions.

data_flow: More than 10 real-time data streams feed AWARE, which produces roadway and curbside predictions for operations, police, and ground transport teams. Separately, work-order history, sensor data, and condition information feed the asset-health foundation, which powers the Resource Scheduling Optimizer and asset-manager cockpit to dispatch technicians and guide asset decisions.
business_outcome: Within just over a year, DFW used the platforms to reduce peak congestion by roughly 24%, cut reaction times from tens of minutes to seconds, raise maintenance efficiency by more than 20%, and increase maintenance completion from around 80% to over 90%, while transferring ownership of the platforms to DFW teams.

architecture_clues: AWARE fuses more than 10 real-time data streams and generates over 120,000 predictions a day across 26 key roadways.
The Resource Scheduling Optimizer combines workforce availability with maintenance needs in a technician application and optimized schedule.
The asset-health foundation brings together work-order history, sensor data, and condition into a single view of each asset's health.
The maintenance platform was proven first in facilities maintenance and HVAC in three terminals and is scaling to all terminals and passenger-facing systems.
BCG initially led product delivery before the platforms became owned and operated by DFW.
